memory_notes: Pillow (PIL) 12.3.0 in-process; no browser binary, no subprocess. 5 warm renders kept RSS flat. PNG output is 51,164 bytes vs R-A's 377,459 bytes (7x smaller).
packaging_notes: R-B requires only Pillow (already a project dep via existing test/install path) and a bundled font (Segoe UI on Windows; the same font chain ships in default LibreOffice / Noto on Linux/macOS). R-A requires the full chromium browser binary (~150 MB compressed) installed via 'playwright install chromium' on first run and on every CI runner. For a local-first desktop app that explicitly does NOT want to ship a browser (plan section 42 motivation), R-B's ~12 MB Pillow install is the right footprint.
implementation_notes: R-B's design source IS an SVG file (spikes/renderer/candidate_b_svg/template.svg) committed as the human-readable layout source of truth. The Pillow rasterisation in this spike is throwaway; A14 dio 2 (production renderer) will swap it for a real SVG library (cairosvg or resvg) — that swap is a one-line call change. A14 dio 2 produces: (a) the production template.svg derived from the spike's reference, (b) the production renderer (infrastructure/rendering/selected_renderer.py) that does the one-line SVG-to-PNG conversion, (c) the Port interface (ports/rendering.py) and the application use-case (application/rendering/render_post.py) per plan section 43-44. R-B's overflow detection is programmatic and one-comparison (wrapped_height vs budget), which is what plan section 44 calls LAYOUT_VALIDATION_ERROR. R-B's text measurement uses font.getlength() directly on the font file, no browser, no JS, sub-millisecond per glyph.
decision: R-B wins. R-B is selected as the A14 production renderer. Concrete reasoning: (1) packaging — Pillow is already a project dep; chromium binary is a hard 'no' for the local-first desktop app per plan section 42. (2) performance — 48.5ms warm vs 745ms warm for R-A, 51 KB vs 377 KB PNG. (3) text measurement — font.getlength() is a pure-Python primitive that gives the same numbers as the browser DOM measurement, with no browser in the loop, so plan section 44's LAYOUT_VALIDATION_ERROR check is a single comparison. (4) implementation — A14 dio 2 swap from Pillow prototype to a real SVG library is a one-line change; the production deliverable is the template.svg layout spec, not the Python rasteriser. R-A stays in the repo as a future reference for scenarios that need rich CSS (multi-column, hover states, interactive preview) — for static PNG export it is the wrong tool. The R-B spike is throwaway code; the R-B production artefacts (template.svg, ports/rendering.py, infrastructure/rendering/selected_renderer.py) are the next task (A14 dio 2).
